faq.question: Which components do I need to develop on the project

answer.p: The development environment to work on the project requires the following components.

ul.li: A complete Java development environment - we recommend to install Sun JDK 1.4 and JDK 1.5 -. Compatibility to other Java environments, e.g. IBM Jikes are not tested.
The Eclipse IDE - the actual project files are defined for versions 3.x -. Eclipse application can be downloaded from www.eclipse.org. The Eclipse project files are checked in the CVS repository.
If you want to generate the web based documentation you need forrest. Forrest can be downloaded from forrest.apache.org
If you want to extend the web based documentation you need an XML editor for the forrest files and open office for the white papers. Open office can be downloaded from www.openoffice.org

faq.question: How do I install the pmMDA project?

answer.p: We assume you have a basic knowledge of Eclipse and CVS. If not please consult a tutorial about these themes. Very good books and online tutorials can be found about Eclipse. The web site of Eclipse is www.eclipse.org

faq.question: Where do I find the used libraries (jar files)?

answer.p: All librairies used in the projects can be donwloaded as a zip file from the sourceforge project home page. The project team uses the convention that no binary files should be stored in the version management system. Therefore the jar files cannot be found in the repository. A list of all used libraries with their version number is available as a text file in the test lib directory and also in the project documentation.
The pmMDA stays for poor man Model Driven Architecture. It emphazises the goal of the project to provide a pragmantic solution to implement MDA approach in concrete project.

answer.p: Yes. As discribed in the developer's installation guide you must configure a set of JDK and variables. This approach is the recommended way to define portable projects under Eclipse.

Defines the root directory to your JDK 5.0. Java development or runtime kits are defined under Windows/Preferences/Java/Installed JRE.

Defines the tools.jar file in the the JDK 5.0 directory in the lib directory. Variables can be defined in Windows/Preferences/Java/Build Path/Classpath Variables menu. Consult the JDK documentation for the purpose and content of the tools.jar

faq.question: Which Eclipse plugin do you use in the project?

answer.p: Modern IDE simplify a lot the development activities. We recommend using such environments and plugins to augment the efficiency of developers. A fundamental rule in our project is that all artifacts generated with the help of interactive tools can also be generated with command line tools. This approach guarantees batch generation of the deliverables and are the conerstome of a continuous deployment process such as nightly builds.
The project uses the Eclipse environment as development platform for all artifacts. The following features are configured.

dl.dd: Java development environment for all Java related source code development.
C/C++ development environment for all C++ related source code development.
The integrated CVS client is used to communicate with the version management system CVS. The check-in uses the SSH2 mode to authenticate the comitters. The read access uses anonymous login.
The integrated JUnit test client is used to create all units tests.
The velocity plugin is used to edit all Velocity plugin
The velocity plugin is used to edit XML files part of the home page of the project. The home page is generated using forest.
The PMD plugin is used to generate quality code metrics.
The PMD plugin is used to generate quality code metrics.
The Find Bugs plugin is used to generate quality code metrics.

faq.question: A compile error TOOLS not found is displayed?

answer.p: You must define the JDK_TOOLS variable in eclipse environment. See the FAQ entry about variable configuration.

faq.question: Do I need to have a pmMDA project to develop new cartridges?

answer.p: No. You could develop your cartridges without the pmMDA project set up. You only need the pmMDA libraries. Using Eclipse you can debug and test your cartridge before releasing it. The pmMDA has a plugin mechanism for cartridge and no recompile is necessary to support new catridges.
You only need to set up the project if you want to debug the pmMDA kernel functions. For example if you are a developer of the project or want to understand the internals of the pmMDA.

Cartridges can generate artifacts for any programming environments. We know that users developped cartridges for Java - J2SE & J2EE -, C/C++, .NET, SQL, etc. The pmMDA application is written in pure Java to ensure the program can be run under various operation systems. The pmMDA group thinks this advantage is very important and will only provide support for cartridges written in Java.
But feel free to port the pmMDA to other development environments. Let us know about and we will put a link to your project on our site.

faq.question: How can I find out which ant target are available?

answer.p: Execute Ant with ant -p to see a description of the available targets. For more details consult the Ant documentation.
Please remember that development of the pmMDA core is supported through the Eclispe projects. The Ant targets are provided to generate the distribution and the test cases.

faq.question: How can I run the documentation target within the ant goal without errors.

answer.p: You need first to install the official forrest release version 0.6. Second you must add the validator library to your ant libraries in the lib directory. The validator library xml-commons-resolver.jaris part of the forrest distribution.
